# The National Park Of Eryri (Snowdonia)

Scroll down


## One of Britain's breathing spaces...

A place for peace and tranquillity within a diverse, historic and vibrant landscape

Situated on the west coast of Britain, covering 823 square miles of diverse landscapes, Eryri National Park (Snowdonia) is a living, working area, and is home to over 26,000 people. As well as being the largest National Park in Wales, Eryri (Snowdonia) boasts the highest mountain in England and Wales.

## Key activities

Whether you’re planning a family holiday, an adventure with friends or a romantic getaway, there’s plenty of things to do in Eryri (Snowdonia).

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Beicio-%C2%A9VW-copy-600x400.jpg)

Activity

### Biking , Activity

The Park's rugged and mountainous landscape makes it a perfect place for both mountain and road biking.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Aurora-Above-Trawsfynydd-600x400.jpg)

Activity

### Stargazing , Activity

The Park was designated an International Dark Sky Reserve in 2015, making it a truly unique place for stargazing.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Mynedfa-Castell-Harlech-%C2%A9VW-600x400.jpg)

Activity

### Indulging in History , Activity

From prehistoric stone monuments to medieval castles and abbeys, Eryri's (Snowdonia's) landscape is a wealth of history and heritage.

![Special qualities](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Cwch-Llyn-%C2%A9APCE-1920x1080.jpg)

## Special qualities

9 reasons why Eryri (Snowdonia) is a special place

Community – Eryri’s (Snowdonia’s) communities are scattered over five towns and twenty-four villages each with a strong identity that is deeply felt by its inhabitants and visitors.

The Welsh language – The vibrancy of the Welsh language in Eryri (Snowdonia) is one of its defining factors. It is evident in the names given to places and wildlife. The language is the mother tongue of the majority of the Park’s communities.

Landscapes – Eryri (Snowdonia) features nine mountain ranges, fifteen peaks above 3000 feet, twenty-three miles of sweeping coastline and 3000mm of rainfall per year – all within 823 square miles.

Inspiration for the arts – Eryri (Snowdonia) is a place which has inspired some of the nation’s most notable culture, folklore, art, literature and music; an influence which continues across all creative pursuits to the present day.

Tranquillity and solitude – Tranquillity still prevails in many parts of Eryri (Snowdonia), both during the day, in its large, remote and rugged mountain ranges; and at night, when the vast, awe-inspiring dark skies are revealed.

Recreation opportunities – Eryri (Snowdonia) is great for adventure and exploring. It has endless opportunities to be active and learn new skills. Everest teams use Eryri to practice their climbing skills.

Historic landscapes – Eryri (Snowdonia) is a backdrop to a rich history and heritage. From stone monuments to medieval castles, the landscape is teeming with history and tradition ready for you to explore.

Renowned geology – It might be hard to believe, but, 500 million years ago Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) was submerged in seawater. Shell fossils have been found at its summit giving us a better understanding of how the landscape of Eryri (Snowdonia) was formed.

Internationally important species and habitats – Eryri (Snowdonia) is home to numerous species of animals, insects, plants and fungi of international importance. Among the rarest of species is Lili’r Wyddfa (Snowdon Lily) – a plant found only at the highest peaks.

## Did you know?

Welsh is the mother tongue of the vast majority of Eryri's (Snowdonia's) communities. It is spoken by 58% of the Park's population.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Windsurfing-4-%C2%A9VW-900x600.jpg)

Windsurfing is one of the many outdoor activities that Eryri (Snowdonia) has to offer.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/lilir-wyddfa-900x600.png)

Lili’r Wyddfa is the rarest plant in Eryri (Snowdonia).

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/076_ffN_96-900x600.jpg)

Eryri's (Snowdonia's) wardens have extensive knowledge of the landscape.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Stondin-Jam-a-Chutney-%C2%A9VW-900x600.jpg)

The towns and communities of Eryri (Snowdonia) are often bustling with culture.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Danddaear-%C2%A9VW-900x600.jpg)

Exploring Eryri (Snowdonia) underground is just as thrilling as exploring overground.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Llennyrch-footpath-image-4-900x600.jpg)

Ancient Celtic rainforests scatter the landscape throughout Eryri (Snowdonia).

# Enjoying Eryri (Snowdonia)

Eryri’s (Snowdonia’s) landscape is unique. The nine mountain ranges cover approximately 52% of the Park and include many peaks that are over 3,000 feet (915m). Apart from the beauty and charm of its high mountains, Eryri (Snowdonia) is a delightfully varied landscape of steep river gorges, waterfalls and green valleys. Oak, ash, rowan and hazel woodlands are found scattered throughout the Park whilst the beautiful Dyfi, Mawddach and Dwyryd estuaries contribute to the overall diversity of the landscape.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Llyn-Idwal-ar-Glyderau-%C2%A9VW-1920x1080.jpg)

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/NVW-C15-1920-00341-580x580.jpg)

### Getting around

Bus services are the best way to experience Eryri (Snowdonia). The Sherpa’r Wyddfa shuttle service circles the base of Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) – a great way to access the peak’s footpaths and its surrounding communities. You could also try your hand at cycling the many routes that run through the Park.

For a more unique travel method, try the Ffestiniog and Welsh Highland Narrow Gauge Railways.

![](https://nationalparks.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/Beicio-%C2%A9APCE-580x580.jpg)

### Getting there

Aim for Llandudno or Shrewsbury if travelling by train. From here, inland services such as the Conwy Valley Line and the Cambrian Line can take you all across the Park.

If travelling by car, aim towards the A55 from the North and the M54 from the South.

Welcome

Covering a total of 823 square miles, Eryri is Wales’ largest National Park. Home to over 26,000 people, Eryri’s landscape is steeped with culture, history, and heritage, where the Welsh language is part of the day-to-day fabric of the area.

Nearly 4 million people visit Eryri every year to explore its towering peaks and breath-taking valleys, find tranquillity in its lesser-trodden paths and discover its extensive recreation opportunities.

**Eryri National Park**
_Parc Cenedlaethol Eryri_( [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_language "Welsh language")) | | [IUCN category](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IUCN_protected_area_categories "IUCN protected area categories") V (protected landscape/seascape)[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-1) | | Location | [Conwy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conwy_County_Borough "Conwy County Borough") and [Gwynedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwynedd "Gwynedd") (Wales) | | Coordinates | ![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/WMA_button2b.png/20px-WMA_button2b.png)[52°54′N3°51′W﻿ / ﻿52.900°N 3.850°W﻿ / 52.900; -3.850](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Snowdonia¶ms=52_54_N_3_51_W_region:GB_type:landmark_source:dewiki_dim:48km) | | Area | 823sqmi (2,130km2) | | Established | 1951 | | Governingbody | Snowdonia National Park Authority | | Website | [eryri.gov.wales](https://eryri.gov.wales/) | | [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/3/36/Eryri_National_Park_logo.png/120px-Eryri_National_Park_logo.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eryri_National_Park_logo.png) | | | **Snowdonia**, or **Eryri** (Welsh:[\[ɛˈrəri\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Welsh "Help:IPA/Welsh")[Play audio](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/0/0c/Eryri.ogg/Eryri.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Eryri.ogg "File:Eryri.ogg")), is a mountainous region and [national park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_parks_of_the_United_Kingdom "National parks of the United Kingdom") in [North Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Wales "North Wales"). It contains all 15 mountains in Wales [over 3000 feet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_3000s "Welsh 3000s") high, including the country's highest, [Snowdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdon "Snowdon") (_Yr Wyddfa_), which is 1,085 metres (3,560ft) tall. These peaks are all part of the [Snowdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdon_Massif "Snowdon Massif"), [Glyderau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyderau "Glyderau"), and [Carneddau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carneddau "Carneddau") ranges in the north of the region. The lower [Moelwynion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moelwynion "Moelwynion") and [Moel Hebog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moel_Hebog "Moel Hebog") ranges lie immediately to the south. The national park has an area of 823 square miles (2,130km2), and covers most of central and southern [Gwynedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwynedd "Gwynedd") and the western part of [Conwy County Borough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conwy_County_Borough "Conwy County Borough"). This is much larger than the area traditionally considered Snowdonia, and in addition to the five ranges above includes the [Rhinogydd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhinogydd "Rhinogydd"), [Cadair Idris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadair_Idris "Cadair Idris"), and [Aran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aran_Fawddwy "Aran Fawddwy") ranges and the [Dyfi Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyfi_hills "Dyfi hills"). It also includes most of the coast between [Porthmadog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porthmadog "Porthmadog") and [Aberdyfi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aberdyfi "Aberdyfi"). The park was the first of the three [national parks of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_parks_of_Wales "National parks of Wales") to be designated, in October 1951, and the third in the UK after the [Peak District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peak_District "Peak District") and [Lake District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_District "Lake District"), which were established in April and May 1951, respectively. The park received 3.89 million visitors in 2015.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-2) ## Toponymy \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Snowdonia&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Toponymy")\] The name "Snowdon" means "snow hill" and is derived from the [Old English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_English "Old English") elements _"snāw_" and _"dūn_", the latter meaning "hill".[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-3) It is first recorded as _Snawdune_ in 1095.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-:3-4) "Snowdonia" is derived from the name of the mountain and is first recorded in 1284, but there is no evidence it survived in common use until it was re-popularised in the 19th century.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-:3-4)[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-5) The Welsh name of the mountain is __Yr Wyddfa__, and is unrelated to the name of the area. _Eryri_ is first recorded in 1191. It likely derived from _eryr_, meaning "ridge", with the collective form _eryri_ referring to the area around Snowdon. A popular interpretation is that the name means "place of the eagle", as _eryr_ also means "eagle" and the two meanings are probably [cognate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognate "Cognate").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-:3-4)[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-6)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-9) ## Extent \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Snowdonia&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Extent")\] Before the designation of the national park in 1951, "Snowdonia" was generally used to refer to a smaller upland area of northern [Gwynedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwynedd "Gwynedd") centred on the Snowdon [massif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massif "Massif"). F. J. North, writing in 1949, states that "When the Committee delineated provisional boundaries \[of the national park\], they included areas some distance beyond Snowdonia proper".[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-10) In [George Borrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Borrow "George Borrow")'s 1862 _Wild Wales_, he states that "Snowdon or Eryri is no single hill, but a mountainous region, the loftiest part of which \[is\] called Y Wyddfa", making a distinction between the summit of the mountain and the surrounding massif.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-11) The 1925 _Mountains of Snowdonia_ by H. Carr & G. Lister defines "Eryri" as "composed of the two [cantrefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantref "Cantref") of [Arfon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cantref_Arfon "Cantref Arfon") and [Arllechwedd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arllechwedd "Arllechwedd"), and the two commotes of Nant Conwy and [Eifionydd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eifionydd "Eifionydd")",[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-12) which corresponds to [Caernarfonshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caernarfonshire "Caernarfonshire") with the exception of the [Creuddyn Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creuddyn_Peninsula "Creuddyn Peninsula") and the south-west of the [Llŷn Peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ll%C5%B7n_Peninsula "Llŷn Peninsula"). A 1941 article by Thomas Cotterill Warrington in the [Geographical Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographical_Association "Geographical Association")'s _Geography_ journal described "Snowdonia" as a "tourist's or mountaineer's term" and defined it as: > the district of which [Pen y Gwryd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pen-y-Gwryd "Pen-y-Gwryd") is the centre. It is bounded by the [Conway valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Conwy "River Conwy") as far as the Fairy Glen, thence by the [Lledr Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lledr_Valley "Lledr Valley") to [Dolwyddelen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolwyddelan "Dolwyddelan"), then over the hills to the [Ffestiniog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ffestiniog "Ffestiniog") Valley and [Portmadoc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porthmadog "Porthmadog"), and from that point by the road to [Carnarvon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caernarfon "Caernarfon") by [Dolbenmaen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolbenmaen "Dolbenmaen") and [Llanllyfni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Llanllyfni "Llanllyfni"). In the same article, "Eryri" is defined as the above area and the highlands between [Bwlch Mawr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bwlch_Mawr "Bwlch Mawr") and [Yr Eifl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yr_Eifl "Yr Eifl"), with reference to the definition given in _The Mountains of Snowdonia_.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdonia#cite_note-:2-13) In the 1946 book _National Parks for Britain_, Henry Chessell defines _Snowdonia_ is the "mountain district of [Carnarvonshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnarvonshire "Carnarvonshire")", including the [Snowdon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowdon_Massif "Snowdon Massif"), [Carneddau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carneddau "Carneddau"), [Glyderau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyderau "Glyderau"), [Moel Hebog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moel_Hebog "Moel Hebog"), and [Moelwynion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moelwynion "Moelwynion") massifs.
